source_text: Διὰ τοῦτο τὴν γλῶτταν ἀπέτεμεν, ἵνα ἀποστερηθέντες τῆς φωνῆς, ἧς ἀπήλαυον οἱ τοῦ μάρτυρος μαθηταὶ, καὶ τῆς συμβουλῆς ἐκπεσόντες, καὶ τῆς παραινέσεως ἐρη μωθέντες, δειλότεροι γένωνται, καὶ πρὸς τὴν προτέραν ἀγωνίαν ἐπανέλθωσιν, οὐκ ἔχοντες τὸν ἐπαλείφοντα, οὐδὲ τὸν διεγείροντα καὶ καθοπλίζοντα. γʹ. Καὶ σκόπει μοι τὴν κακουργίαν. Ἡρώδης μὲν ἀπέτεμε τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου· οὗτος δὲ οὐχὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν, ἀλλὰ τὴν γλῶτταν μόνην. Τί δήποτε; Διὰ πολλὴν κακουργίαν καὶ σκαιότητα. Ἂν ἀποτέμω τὴν κεφαλὴν, φησὶ, καὶ ἀποθάνῃ, ἀπελεύσεται οὐχ ὁρῶν τὴν ἀπώλειαν τῶν ἑαυτοῦ ἀδελφῶν· ἐγὼ δὲ αὐτὸν βούλομαι στῆσαι μάρτυρα τῶν πτωμάτων καὶ τῆς συμφορᾶς τῶν οἰκείων στρατιωτῶν, ἵν', ὑπὸ τῆς ὀδύνης ἄγχηται καταπίπτοντας μὲν ὁρῶν, χεῖρα δὲ ὀρέγειν μὴ δυνάμενος, καὶ τὸ συμβουλεῦσαι ταῦτα ἅπερ καὶ πρότερον οὐκ ἔχων, τῆς φωνῆς μετὰ τῆς γλώττης ἐκκοπείσης. Ἀλλ' ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν, τὸ σόφισμα τοῦτο εἰς τὴν ἐκείνου περιέτρεψε κεφαλὴν, καὶ οὐ μόνον συμβουλῆς οὐκ ἀπεστέρησεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ πλείονος αὐτοὺς ἐποίησεν ἀπολαῦσαι παραινέσεως, καὶ πνευματικωτέρας μετασχεῖν διδασκαλίας. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ τοῦτο ἐκράτησε, καλεῖται λοιπὸν ἐπὶ τὴν τομὴν ὁ ἰατρὸς, καὶ δήμιος ἀντὶ ἰατροῦ γίγνεται, οὐχὶ τὸ νενοσηκὸς διορθούμενος μέλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ ὑγιαῖνον διαφθείρων· καὶ τὴν γλῶτταν ἐξελὼν, οὐκ ἴσχυσεν αὐτῇ συνεξελεῖν καὶ τὴν φωνήν· ἀλλ' ἡ μὲν τῆς σαρκὸς ἐξεκόπτετο γλῶττα, ἡ δὲ τῆς χάριτος ἐφίπτατο τῷ στόματι τοῦ μακαρίου· καὶ ἡ μὲν φύσις τὸ οἰκεῖον ἠφίει μέλος, τοῦ σιδήρου τοῦτο καταναγκάζοντος, ἡ δὲ χάρις συνεκπεσεῖν αὐτῇ τὴν φωνὴν οὐκ εἴασεν· ὅθεν λοιπὸν πνευματικωτέρας ἀπήλαυον οἱ μαθηταὶ διδασκαλίας, οὐκ ἀνθρωπίνῃ φωνῇ καθάπερ τὰ πρότερα ἀκούοντες, ἀλλὰ θείᾳ τινὶ, καὶ πνευματικῇ, καὶ μείζονι τῆς φύσεως τῆς ἡμετέρας· καὶ πάντες συνέτρεχον, ἄνωθεν ἄγγελοι, κάτωθεν ἄνθρωποι, ἕκαστος χωρὶς γλώττης στόμα ἰδεῖν ἐπιθυμοῦντες, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι φθεγγομένου οὕτως. Καὶ γὰρ ἦν ὄντως θαυμαστὸν καὶ παράδοξον στόμα ἄνευ γλώττης φθεγγόμενον, πολλὴν μὲν τῷ διαβόλῳ φέρον αἰσχύνην, πολλὴν δὲ τῷ μάρτυρι δόξαν, μεγάλην δὲ τοῖς μαθηταῖς παράκλησιν καὶ ὑπομονῆς ὑπόθεσιν. Καὶ γὰρ ἔθος τῷ Θεῷ τοιοῦτον ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ ἀρχῆς, ἅπερ ἂν καθ' ἡμῶν ὁ διάβολος ῥάψῃ, ταῦτα εἰς τὴν ἐκείνου τρέπειν κεφαλὴν, καὶ ὑπὲρ τῆς ἡμετέρας κατασκευάζειν σωτηρίας. Σκόπει δέ· ἐξέβαλεν ἐκεῖνος τοῦ παραδείσου τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ ἀνέῳξεν αὐτῷ τὸν οὐρανὸν ὁ Θεός· ἀπήλασεν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖνος τῆς ἀρχῆς τῆς ἐν τῇ γῇ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τῷ βασιλικῷ τὴν φύσιν ἐνίδρυσε τὴν ἡμετέραν. Οὕτως ἀεὶ μείζονα δίδωσιν ἀγαθὰ, ὧν ὁ διάβολος ἀποστερεῖν ἐπιχειρεῖ. Ποιεῖ δὲ τοῦτο, ἐκεῖνόν τε ὀκνηρότερον ἐν ταῖς καθ' ἡμῶν κατασκευάζων ἐπιβουλαῖς, ἡμᾶς δὲ παιδεύων μηδέποτε αὐτοῦ δεδοικέναι τὰ μηχανήματα· ὃ δὴ καὶ ἐνταῦθα γέγονεν ἐπὶ τοῦ μάρτυρος. Ἧς γὰρ προσεδόκησε φωνῆς ἀποστερήσειν αὐτὸν, πολλῷ μείζονα καὶ σεμνοτέραν αὐτῷ ἐχαρίσατο ὁ Θεός. Οὐ γὰρ ἦν ἴσον μετὰ γλώττης φθέγγεσθαι, καὶ χωρὶς γλώττης· τὸ μὲν γὰρ ἀκόλουθον ἦν, καὶ κοινὸν ἅπασι, τὸ δὲ ὑπὲρ τὴν φύσιν, καὶ αὐτοῦ ἴδιον ἐγένετο μόνου.
thought_title: The devil cuts out the tongue; grace supplies a greater voice
orientation: The devil, reasoning that killing Romanus would only encourage his disciples, decides instead to cut out his tongue so that he can no longer exhort them.
pass_a_gloss: For this reason he cut off the tongue, in order that, having been deprived of the voice which the disciples of the martyr were enjoying, and having fallen away from counsel, and having been made desolate of exhortation, they might become more cowardly, and might return to their former anguish, not having the one who anoints them, nor the one who rouses and arms them. 3. And observe for me the wickedness. Herod cut off the head of John; but this one cut off not the head, but only the tongue. Why ever? Because of much wickedness and perversity. If I cut off the head, he says, and he dies, he will depart not seeing the destruction of his own brothers; but I wish to set him up as a witness of the corpses and of the calamity of his own soldiers, in order that he may be choked by pain, seeing them falling, but not being able to stretch out a hand, and not having the ability to counsel these things which he also formerly did, since the voice has been cut out together with the tongue. But the one who catches the wise in their craftiness turned this scheme back upon that one's head, and not only did he not deprive them of counsel, but he also made them enjoy more exhortation, and share in more spiritual teaching. For when this prevailed, the physician is called next to the cutting, and becomes an executioner instead of a physician, not correcting the diseased member, but destroying the healthy one; and having removed the tongue, he was not able to remove also the voice together with it; but the tongue of the flesh was being cut out, while the grace was hovering over the mouth of the blessed one; and nature was letting go its own member, since the iron was forcing this, but grace did not allow the voice to fall out together with it; whence from then on the disciples enjoyed more spiritual teaching, hearing not with a human voice as before, but with a certain divine and spiritual voice, and one greater than our nature; and all were running together, from above angels, from below humans, each one desiring to see a mouth without a tongue, and to hear one speaking in this way. For truly it was wonderful and paradoxical, a mouth without a tongue speaking, bringing much shame to the devil, and much glory to the martyr, and great consolation to the disciples and an occasion of endurance. For such is the custom of God from above and from the beginning: whatever things the devil sews against us, these things he turns upon that one's head, and prepares them for our salvation. Observe then: that one cast the human being out of paradise, and God opened heaven to him; that one drove him away from the rule on the earth, and God gave him the kingdom of the heavens, and established our nature on the royal throne. Thus he always gives greater goods than those which the devil attempts to deprive us of. And he does this, making that one more hesitant in his plots against us, and teaching us never to fear his devices; which indeed also happened here in the case of the martyr. For the voice which he expected to deprive him of, God granted him a much greater and more august one. For it was not equal to speak with a tongue and to speak without a tongue; for the one was natural, and common to all, but the other was above nature, and became his alone.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'tongue' for γλῶττα; the verb is aorist, rendered as simple past.
The passive participle conveys deprivation of exhortation; 'desolate' captures the emptiness left by the loss.
ἐπαλείφω means to anoint or rub on, used metaphorically for encouragement; the participle is substantival.

choices.english: to set him up as a witness
choices.why: στῆσαι means to make stand or set up; μάρτυρα here is a witness to the calamity, not the technical 'martyr' sense, so I use 'witness' to avoid confusion.
rejected: to make him a martyr of the corpses
to station him as a witness

choices.why: ὑπόθεσις here means a starting point or occasion that gives rise to endurance, not a foundation or basis.

choices.english: turned this scheme back upon that one's head
choices.why: ἐκείνου refers to the devil, the one whose scheme it was; the idiom means the scheme recoiled on its deviser. The checker's suggestion that it refers to Romanus is not supported by the context, where God turns the devil's plots against the devil himself.
rejected: turned this scheme back upon the martyr's head
turned this scheme back upon Romanus's head

bible_refs.note: ὁ δρασσόμενος τοὺς σοφοὺς ἐν τῇ πανουργίᾳ αὐτῶν

pass_b_english: For this reason he cut off the tongue, so that the martyr’s disciples, deprived of the voice they had been enjoying, and having fallen away from counsel, and having been made desolate of exhortation, might become more cowardly and return to their former anxiety, since they no longer had the one who anoints them, nor the one who rouses and arms them.

And observe the wickedness. Herod cut off the head of John the Baptist, but this one cut off not the head, but only the tongue. Why? Because of great wickedness and perversity. “If I cut off his head,” he says, “and he dies, he will depart without seeing the destruction of his own brothers. But I want to set him up as a witness of the corpses and the calamity of his fellow soldiers, so that he may be choked by grief as he watches them fall, unable to stretch out a hand, and no longer able to give the counsel he gave before, since his voice has been cut out along with his tongue.”

But the One who catches the wise in their craftiness turned this scheme back upon that one’s head, and not only did He not deprive them of counsel, but He made them enjoy even more exhortation and share in more spiritual teaching. For when this was decided, the physician is summoned for the cutting, and the executioner takes the place of the physician, not correcting the diseased member but destroying the healthy one. And when he removed the tongue, he was not able to remove the voice along with it. The tongue of flesh was cut out, but the grace hovered over the blessed man’s mouth. Nature released its own member, as the iron forced it, but grace did not allow the voice to fall out with it. From then on the disciples enjoyed more spiritual teaching, hearing not a human voice as before, but a divine and spiritual voice, greater than our nature. And everyone ran together—angels from above, humans from below—each one longing to see a mouth without a tongue and to hear it speaking in this way.

For it was truly wondrous and extraordinary: a mouth speaking without a tongue, bringing great shame to the devil, great glory to the martyr, and great encouragement to the disciples, an occasion of endurance. For it is God’s custom from the beginning: whatever the devil stitches together against us, He turns it back upon that one’s head and makes it serve our salvation.

Consider: the devil cast the human being out of paradise, and God opened heaven to him. The devil drove him from his rule on earth, and God gave him the kingdom of heaven and seated our nature on the royal throne. So God always gives greater goods than those the devil tries to deprive us of. He does this to make the devil more hesitant in his plots against us, and to teach us never to fear his schemes. This is what happened here with the martyr. For the voice the devil expected to deprive him of, God granted him a much greater and more august one. It was not the same thing to speak with a tongue and to speak without a tongue. The former was natural and common to all; the latter was beyond nature and became his alone.

last_rejected.quote: since his voice has been cut out along with his tongue
last_rejected.source_quote: τῆς φωνῆς μετὰ τῆς γλώττης ἐκκοπείσης
last_rejected.why: This is the devil's speech; 'since' makes it the devil's reason, but the Greek is a genitive absolute: the voice was cut out with the tongue.
last_rejected.fix: his voice having been cut out along with his tongue
last_rejected.ruling: Genitive absolute 'τῆς φωνῆς...ἐκκοπείσης' is causal/temporal; 'since' captures this adverbial function correctly in context.

last_rejected.why: μαθηταὶ here means followers/companions, not formal disciples; implies wrong relationship.
last_rejected.ruling: μαθηταὶ normally means disciples; 'followers/companions' is a preference, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: πτωμάτων means 'falls' (moral lapses), not dead bodies; changes devil's scheme entirely.
last_rejected.ruling: πτωμάτων means corpses/fallen bodies; 'moral lapses' is unsupported and changes the devil's scheme.
